project_name: Unnamed Mason County hyperscale data center campus
status_detail: City of Maysville/Mason County public information page says Mason County Fiscal Court Ordinance 26-03 approved a rezoning application related to a data center development in unincorporated Mason County. The Fiscal Court held first reading May 12, 2026 and second reading/consideration May 22, 2026 for rezoning 28 properties, about 2,080 acres north of Germantown Road, to I-3 Rural Industrial for a proposed data center project. The JPC had approved the proposed development plan with a condition on April 22, 2026.
notes: Applicant/developer identity not publicly disclosed in reviewed sources. News reports describe the preliminary plan as a six-building hyperscale campus near Big Pond Pike, Germantown Road and Valley Pike Road, with construction planned for summer 2027; official page links underlying application, development plan, maps, findings, and transcripts.

project_name: Paducah American Energy Hub Data Center
aliases: Paducah DOE Site AI data center campus
status_detail: McCracken County official page hosts the Paducah American Energy Hub/Data Center information and fact sheet. The fact sheet lists McCracken County, KY location, 600-acre data center footprint, commercial operation as early as 2028, and data center capacity up to 1,800 MW. Project materials say Brookfield would build/finance/operate the data center, NextEra would supply energy infrastructure, with Big Rivers, Jackson Purchase Energy Cooperative, and Paducah Power System involved. NextEra announcement describes a $100B privately funded data center campus at DOE's Paducah Site.
notes: FAQ says the project was selected in July 2026 after DOE's November 2025 request for offers, remains in early stages, and technical/environmental analyses are underway. Greater Paducah EDC states the data center is anticipated to consume about 1.8 GW and be operational by 2028; NextEra release says fully constructed in 2032 with over 1.2 GW compute capacity.

project_name: Unnamed Ekron / Joe Prather Highway data center
aliases: IT infrastructure facility at 25025 Joe Prather Hwy
status_detail: Local news reported Meade County officials unanimously blocked a data center after a proposed zone change for 135 acres just off Joe Prather Highway from Agriculture 2/Residential 1 to Light Industrial for an IT infrastructure facility. County later posted Ordinance 2025-07, a temporary moratorium on accepting or processing applications related to IT infrastructure facilities including data centers, with first reading dated December 9, 2025.
notes: Project address appears in petition/third-party tracker as 25025 Joe Prather Hwy, Ekron, KY; developer not identified in official/news sources reviewed. Moratorium is official county evidence of data center regulatory response after the rejected rezoning.

aliases: Mercer County proposed data center campus
status_detail: Mercer County Planning & Zoning official page lists proposed county/city zoning ordinances related to data centers, including second draft heard July 23, 2026 and first draft heard April 28, 2026. News coverage says Burgin is weighing annexation of several hundred acres of farmland, clearing the way for a proposed data center campus known as Project Bluegrass; WKYT reported on July 28, 2026 that Mercer Fiscal Court approved a motion for a data center moratorium requiring a follow-up meeting, and that a magistrate said two possible data centers were under consideration.
notes: Official county materials establish active data-center zoning work but do not name a specific applicant. Project Bluegrass name and Burgin annexation/site details come from local news; developer not identified in reviewed sources. Also preserve note that at least one other possible data center was reported by WKYT but not separately named or located.
